text: Because the Bankruptcy Code does not define adequate information, prepackaged plans risk inadequate disclosure, creditor challenge, and unusable prepetition votes that force the case into the longer ordinary Chapter 11 confirmation procedure.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Christoph Henkel, Contingent Capital with Sequential Triggers (2011). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=1908473
abstract: Given this shortcoming, the agreement may be challenged by creditors. In many cases, the prepetition votes cannot be utilized, forcing the reorganization into the ordinary and much longer plan confirmation procedure under Chapter 11.
